stories.headline: Juniper Ridge starts its 5A title defense without seven regulars
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Bryce Seaver lost one match last season. He went 35-1, mostly at No. 2 doubles, and he graduated in June with six other Juniper Ridge regulars, Rafael Rivera at first singles and Ricardo Rodriguez (33-3) among them.
Juniper Ridge went 18-0 in the Kajaani on the way to the 5A title in October, and it starts the defense Monday at Liberty Hill.

Three players who won 28 matches apiece are back: seniors Ezekiel Amoore and Deon Rennick and junior Joshua Butcher, who spent most of their time in doubles. At Saturday's last practice before the opener, coach Ray Okafor put all three at the top of the singles order in turn and reset it between drills.
"I don't have a one yet," Okafor said. "Zeke, Deon and Josh all think it's them. Levi probably does too, and he's the only one of them who never lost."
Levi Chesnut, a sophomore, went 16-0 as a freshman at second and third singles. Four freshmen are on this year's roster, Dimitri Kimball among them.
Juniper Ridge plays four duals in four days: at Liberty Hill, then home against Pacersburg and Westfield Friends, then the Kajaani opener Thursday at Cedar Exchange.

stories.headline: Carroway sorts seven freshmen before Wednesday's opener
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: "Seven freshmen," Carroway coach Linda Haverkamp said, counting the names on her clipboard a second time. "Some of them will be playing doubles by Friday."

Carroway lost the 3A state final in October and graduated both players who shared first singles, Asher Barrett and Bronson Koontz. Haverkamp named Uwe Fiebich and Rashad McCloud as two of the freshmen pushing for doubles spots.

Senior Luke Palm (23-4) and junior James Stacy (20-5) played almost all of their matches in doubles. Junior Jasper Kuroda went 14-4, mostly at second singles, and senior Max Callender went 9-3 at third.
Carroway opens Wednesday at home against Pacersburg. Juniper League play starts Aug. 8 at Ostrander Union, last year's runner-up.

stories.headline: County by county: Silton Ridge, Vesper and the Desert Sky
body: RIMROCK COUNTY

Vesper and Silton Ridge. Silton Ridge (14-2) won the Desert Sky and Vesper (12-4) was second, and both went out in the state quarterfinals. Vesper keeps sophomore Taras Piątek, who won 26 of 29 matches as a freshman, almost all at No. 1 and No. 2 doubles. Silton Ridge has nine seniors and a junior, William Lemke, who went 21-5 in doubles. The two do not meet in the opening two weeks.
Covenant. The PAA champion (11-1) plays three of its first five duals on the road, two of them in league play.

Dry Lake. It was second in the Fiesta with four underclassmen, juniors Lawrence Sullivan and Lorenzo Morlan and sophomores Noah Sorenson and Teagan Combs, playing 31 matches apiece. All four are back.
JUNIPER COUNTY

Altamonte and Senator Gray. Two of the city's three 8A schools open the season against each other Monday at Senator Gray. Altamonte has eight seniors, and Senator Gray's Cranston Diggins (18-10) and John Jensen (20-8), both seniors, shared first singles a year ago.
California Canyons. Hudson Chiu, a junior, played first singles for the DCL champions and went 16-12.
Mt Jacqueline. Ryder Nale went 26-4 as a sophomore, mostly at No. 3 doubles.
High Desert Christian. It went 0-16 in Juniper League play, and the four players who played the most for that team are seniors now.

stories.headline: 12 area duals open the season Monday
body: All 12 are invitationals. Silton Ridge travels to Espoo, a 1A state semifinalist a year ago. Central West End is at Calder, California Canyons at Summervale and Trout Lake at Star Hollow.
